title: Complete 8-Point FFT Flow Graph
description: The full radix-2 decimation-in-time flow graph for N=8 with twelve labeled butterflies, click-to-highlight per butterfly or stage, and output path tracing.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
FFT
Algorithms

learningObjectives: Examine the complete three-stage butterfly structure
Distinguish how pairing span changes while butterfly count does not
Trace the inputs contributing to a single output

controls.label: Any butterfly
controls.purpose: Show its input rows, twiddle, and span

controls.label: Stage label
controls.purpose: Highlight all four butterflies in that stage

controls.label: Output node
controls.purpose: Trace every contributing butterfly and input

simulationModel.modelType: Static data-flow graph with derived topology
equations: stage s pairs rows (base+j, base+j+half) with half = 2^s
assumptions: N = 8, radix-2, decimation in time, in-place
limitations: Shows structure and twiddles; sample values are not propagated through the graph

keyQuestions: What stays constant across stages and what changes?
How many inputs contribute to a single output?
commonMisconceptions: That later stages do more work than earlier ones
That an FFT output depends on only some of the inputs
assessmentOpportunities: State stage count, butterflies per stage, and final span for N = 16
